{{Short description|Swedish mathematician}}
[[File:Tord ganelius.png|thumb| Tord Ganelius]]
'''Tord Hjalmar Ganelius''' (born 23 May 1925 in [[Stockholm]], dead 14 March 2016 in Stockholm) was a [[Sweden|Swedish]] [[mathematician]] and [[professor emeritus]]. He served as Permanent Secretary of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] and was a board member of the [[Nobel Foundation]] from 1981 to 1989.<ref name="vem93">{{cite book|title=Vem är det, svensk biografisk handbok|year=1993|publisher=Nordstedts|isbn=91-1-914072-X|url=https://runeberg.org/vemardet/1993/0368.html|editor=Hans Uddling Katrin Paabo|access-date=17 October 2012|page=368|language=swedish}}</ref><ref name="rsas">[[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]]</ref> His primary research interests were [[holomorphic functions]] and [[approximation theory]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Nationalencyklopedin|year=1992|publisher=Bokförlaget Bra böcker|location=Höganäs|isbn=91-7024-621-1|pages=329|url=http://www.ne.se/tord-ganelius|language=swedish}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Ganelius completed his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1953 at Stockholms Högskola (known as [[Stockholm University]] since 1960) by presenting his dissertation ''Sequences of Analytic Functions and Their Zeros''.<ref>{{cite book
|last=Ganelius
|first=Tord Hjalmar
|title=Sequences of analytic functions and their zeros
|year=1953
|location=Stockholm, London & Paris
|language=Swedish
|id=libris 2660006
}}</ref>

He was an [[associate professor]] at [[Lund University]] in 1953–56 and in 1957 he was appointed Professor of Mathematics at [[University of Gothenburg]], where he served until 1981. During this time he was Dean of the Faculty of Science twice, in 1963–65 and 1977–80.<ref name="vem93"/> In 1972, he was elected a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Memberpages Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences|url=http://www.kva.se/en/contact/Kontakt-sida/?personId=75|accessdate=17 October 2012}}</ref> and he was appointed the permanent secretary in 1981, a position he held until 1989.<ref name="rsas"/> He was a board member of the [[Nobel Foundation]] from 1981 to 1989, and every October he announced the [[Nobel Laureates]] in Physics, Chemistry and Economic Sciences.<ref name="vem93"/>

Tord Ganelius has also been a [[visiting professor]] at the [[University of Washington]] in 1962, [[Cornell University]] in 1967–68 and the [[University of California, San Diego]] in 1972–73.<ref name="vem93"/>

In 1966, Ganelius published the Swedish-language mathematics textbook ”Introduktion till matematiken”, which since 2006 has been available on-line.<ref>{{cite web|title=Introduktion till matematiken|url=http://arkiv.ncm.gu.se/node/1111|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061009123006/http://ncm.gu.se/node/1111|url-status=dead|archive-date=9 October 2006|accessdate=17 October 2012}}</ref>

== Family ==
Tord Ganelius is the son of Hjalmar and Ebba G. In 1951 he married Aggie Hemberg (born 1928).<ref name="vem93"/> They have four children: Per (1952), Truls (1955), Svante (1957) and Aggie Öhman (1963).<ref>{{cite book|title=Vem är vem|year=1965|publisher=Bokförlaget Vem är vem AB|location=Stockholm|url=https://runeberg.org/vemarvem/gota65/0403.html|editor=Paul Harnesk|access-date=17 October 2012|page=379|language=swedish}}</ref>
